title: Year 12 Chemistry Module 5 – Equilibrium and Acid Reactions
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Chemistry Module 5, organised by its four Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: Why don’t some reactions go to completion?

questions.prompt: What type of reaction can proceed in both the forward and reverse directions?
What type of equilibrium has forward and reverse reactions continuing at equal rates?
What must be true of the forward and reverse reaction rates at dynamic equilibrium?
What type of system is required for a chemical equilibrium to be established?
At equilibrium, do reactant and product concentrations have to be equal?
What theory explains reaction rate using successful collisions between particles?
What principle predicts how an equilibrium system responds to a disturbance?
Increasing reactant concentration generally shifts equilibrium towards reactants or products?
For a gaseous equilibrium, increasing pressure favours the side with more or fewer gas particles?
Increasing temperature favours the endothermic or exothermic direction?
Does a catalyst change the position of equilibrium?
Does changing temperature alter the value of the equilibrium constant?

categories.name: What does the equilibrium constant tell us?

questions.prompt: What symbol is commonly used for the equilibrium constant in this course?
A very large equilibrium constant generally favours reactants or products?
A very small equilibrium constant generally favours reactants or products?
What symbol compares the current reaction mixture with the equilibrium condition?
If Q is less than Kₑq, which direction is favoured to reach equilibrium?
questions.answer: The forward direction. Accept: towards products.

questions.prompt: Which factor changes the value of Kₑq: concentration, pressure or temperature?

categories.name: How does solubility relate to equilibrium?

questions.prompt: What term describes a solution containing the maximum dissolved solute at a given temperature?
What solid formed from ions in solution is called?
What constant describes the equilibrium for a sparingly soluble ionic compound?
If the ionic product exceeds Ksp, what is expected to form?
What effect can reduce the solubility of a salt when an ion already present is added?
What traditional food-processing application in the syllabus uses solubility equilibria to remove toxins from foods such as cycad material?
questions.answer: Detoxification by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. Accept: leaching toxins from food.

finalRound.prompt: At dynamic equilibrium, what two reaction rates are equal?
finalRound.answer: The forward and reverse reaction rates.
